recipes.name: Thai Beef Tapa Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 kilo Beef ((use top sirloin or top round), sliced thinly against the grain)
instructions: Make the marinade: Combine all the ingredients in a large bowl or plastic container.
Add beef and marinate in the refrigerator for 4 hours or overnight. Remove beef from marinade, place in a covered plastic container, and store in the freezer until ready to cook.
When ready to cook, thaw beef tapa. Heat oil in a frying pan and cook beef for about 1 to 2 minutes per side. Serve with rice and pickled cucumber, if desired.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo beef short ribs (hiwain nang tig-dadalawang pulgada)

recipes.name: Beef Caldereta Recipe - Mga Sangkap At Paano Lutuin
full_ingredients: 1 kilo beef short ribs (hiwain nang tig-dadalawang pulgada)
1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper (ayon sa panlasa)
instructions: Painitin ang mantika sa isang kasirola na may makapal na ilalim sa katamtaman hanggang malakas na apoy. Unti-unting iluto ang mga hiwa ng baka. Siguraduhing luto ang bawat gilid. Itabi.
Ibalik ang laman sa kasirola. Haluin at lagyan ng asin, paminta, at patis. Ilagay ng dahon ng laurel sa dulo.

Dagdagan ng tubig, peanut butter, at gata. Kapag nagsimulang kumulo ang sarsa, ilagay sa pinakamababa ang apoy ng kalan. Takpan ang kasirola at hayaang kumulo ang kaldereta hanggang sa kaya nang tusukin ng tinidor ang laman ng baka. Kalimitang inaabot ito ng 1 1/2 hanggang 2 oras. Haluin ang kaldereta kada 15 minuto upang hindi masunog ang ilalim ng kasirola. Kung kinakailangan, dagdagan ng kaunting tubig ang sarsa upang hindi ito matuyo.
Iprito ang patatas at karots hanggang maging mapula ang mga ito.
Kapag malambot na ang laman, idagdag ang patatas, karots, pimiento slices, at siling labuyo, kung gagamit. Hayaang maluto ang mga gulay. Timplahan gamit ang asin o patis kung kinakailangan.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo boneless bangus (milkfish) ((use belly fillet), sliced into 1-inch strips)

recipes.name: Bangus Salpicao Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 kilo boneless bangus (milkfish) ((use belly fillet), sliced into 1-inch strips)
instructions: Marinate bangus in garlic and Worcestershire sauce for 1 hour.

Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat then add paprika. Add bangus, skin side down, and fry on both sides until cooked, about 2 to 3 minutes. Season to taste with soy sauce, salt, and pepper. Garnish with toasted garlic and sliced finger chilies, if desired.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo chicken (chopped into serving slices)

recipes.name: Chicken Halang-Halang Recipe
full_ingredients: 3 stalks fresh lemongrass (tanglad) ((white bottom part), lightly pounded)
1 Small green papaya (peeled, deseeded and sliced into wedges)
instructions: In a large pot over medium heat, saute garlic, onion, ginger and turmeric until very fragrant.
Add the chicken fry, stirring occasionally. Cook chicken turns light brown on all sides. Add in fish sauce and continue to stir fry for another minute.
Gradually pour in the coconut milk. Bring to a light simmer. Add the lemongrass and cover the pot, simmer for about 20 minutes or until the chicken is tender. Stir occasionally to prevent curdling.
Add coconut cream and papaya, and continue to simmer for another 10 minutes or until the papaya is cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat. Garnish with chili leaves before serving.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo chicken (naka-slice sa 8 na piraso)

recipes.name: Kalderetang Manok Recipe (Tagalog Version)
full_ingredients: 2 pieces red bell pepper (naka-slice at tinanggalan ng buto)
instructions: Ilagay ang mantika sa mainit na kawali. Igisa ang bawang at sibuyas hanggang sa maging makintab.
Idagdag ang manok at igisa, mga 10 minuto hanggang maging kulay brown.
Ilagay ang tomato sauce at liver spread at pakuluan nang 10 minuto.
Idagdag ang kinadkad na keso, patatas, karot, gisantes, at bell pepper. Timplahan ng asin at paminta. Takpan at hayaang kumulo nang 10 minuto.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo chicken (use bone-in chicken thighs)

recipes.name: Chicken Asado
instructions: Heat the cooking oil in a cooking pot. Saute garlic and onion until browned.
Add the chicken thighs and cook until browned.
Pour the soy sauce and tomato sauce, while stirring constantly. Add the 5-spice powder, star anise, and sugar.
Add 1 to 2 cups of water and let it boil over low heat for about 30 minutes or until the sauce thickens.
Season with salt and ground black pepper. Serve with warm rice. TIP: Do you have a lot of packets of ketchup from fastfood take-outs? You can use this to replace the tomato sauce in this recipe.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo chicken (use thigh-leg part)

recipes.name: Marketman's Chicken Inasal
instructions: Make the marinade: Put chicken in a bowl. Add ginger, garlic, good native vinegar, calamansi, lemongrass, rock salt, and pepper. Marinate 1 hour, stirring to coat chicken pieces evenly.

Meanwhile, make the basting sauce: Melt margarine in a small saucepan over low flame, adding achuete oil for color and cracked black pepper. Barbecue the chicken over medium to low flames until fully cooked, basting chicken several times with the margarine mixture.
Make achuete oil: heat vegetable oil, drop in achuete, and turn the fire off after a minute or so. Let the oil absorb the intense orange-red color and strain away the solids.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo cow cheeks (cut in desired serving sizes)

recipes.name: Mechado ala Alejandrino
full_ingredients: 1/4 kilo pork fat (cut into large cubes)
1 kilo cow cheeks (cut in desired serving sizes)
1 large red apple (peeled, cut into medium cubes (the spongy, not crunchy type))
1 medium red bell pepper (cut into large cubes)
instructions: Sweat onion, garlic, and tomatoes in olive oil. Add bay leaves, peppercorns, salt, and sugar, and cook until onion and tomatoes are quite mushy.
Saute and render the pork fat. Increase fire a bit and add cow cheeks. Allow cow cheeks to cook for about 5 minutes until it turns a darker shade. Add enough stock to cover.
When meat is halfway cooked, add the apple cubes.
Simmer until beef is tender and sauce is thick.
Add bell peppers and olives, and simmer for another 5 minutes.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo flat rice noodles ((you can use any pre-made noodles from the market to save time))

recipes.name: Ilocos-style Miki Noodle Soup
full_ingredients: 1/4 kilo Chicken ((use breast part, cooked), shredded)
8 cups chicken stock ((or 2 chicken cubes to be dissolved in 8 cups of water))
1 kilo flat rice noodles ((you can use any pre-made noodles from the market to save time))
instructions: Saute crushed garlic in preheated oil and add shredded chicken.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a boil.
Add annato powder and simmer until it boils. (If using annatto seeds, boil in hot water and strain the liquid over the broth.)
Add the noodles and cook for 3 to 5 minutes.
Ladle some soup and noodles in a bowl then top with bagnet and a whole egg.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo heart of palm (lumpiang ubod) (julienned and blanched)

recipes.name: Fried Lumpiang Ubod Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 kilo heart of palm (lumpiang ubod) (julienned and blanched)
instructions: Preheat oil in a wok and saute the garlic and onion until transparent.
Add the ubod and the carrots and saute for 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper or if you wish, add one chicken bouillon cube for added flavor. Set aside and let it cool.

On a plate, place the spring roll wrapper and scoop two tablespoons of the ubod and carrots mixture onto the wrapper. Fold the sides and roll until it reaches the end of the spring roll. Mix the cornstarch and water to make a paste. Use it to seal the edge of the wrapper. Repeat the process until you use up all the ubod mixture.
Heat oil in a pan or wok, about 2 to 3 inches deep. Fry each ubod roll for 3 to 5 minutes or until golden brown. Serve immediately with vinegar dipping sauce.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo lamb (use chops)

recipes.name: Lemon Balm Lamb Adobo
instructions: Infuse 1 bay leaf in the oil over medium heat.
Add the lamb. Brown and sear then transfer to a holding container. Set aside.

In the same pan, saute the leeks, garlic, and blue ginger. Add the balsamic vinegar and let boil for a minute without stirring. Place lamb chops back in the pan and add grapes along with soy sauce and nutmeg.
Add the crushed pepper and the remaining bay leaves. Simmer for an hour or until tender, adjust seasoning and let it soak for another hour.
Just before serving whisk in the unsalted butter over medium heat to create a temporary emulsion
Garnish with lemon balm buds and crushed pink peppercorns.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo manila clams (or halaan, cleaned)

recipes.name: Clams and Prawns with Tausi Recipe
instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Saute onion and ginger. Add Chinese black beans.
Add green onions and parsley, if using. Add water and simmer.
Add clams and prawns. Simmer for 3 to 5 minutes until the clams open and the prawns turn pink. Season with salt to taste.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo native chicken native na manok, cut into serving pieces

recipes.name: Tinutungang Manok (Authentic Bicolano Smoked Coconut Chicken Stew)
full_ingredients: 1 kilo native chicken native na manok, cut into serving pieces
1/2 teaspoon crushed black pepper durog na paminta
1 piece long green chili siling haba
2 pieces bird's eye chilies siling labuyo
Warm water for coconut milk extraction 50ml per coconut
instructions: Begin by preparing the smoked coconut milk. Light 2 pieces of charcoal until they become red-hot (500F/260C). Place your freshly grated coconut (niyog) in a heat-resistant bowl and carefully place the hot charcoal pieces on top. Allow some parts of the coconut to burn slightly for about 3-5 minutes, then remove the charcoal. Remember, "Mas maitim ang tusta ng niyog, mas malalim ang lasa ng tinunung" (the darker the coconut is toasted, the deeper the smoky flavor).

Extract the coconut milk in two stages. For the first extract (kakang gata), pour 1 cup of warm water (110F/43C) over the smoked coconut and squeeze firmly through a cheesecloth. Set this thick first extract aside. For the second extract, repeat the process with the remaining warm water. This thinner milk will be used first in cooking.

Heat your wok or deep pan (kawali) to medium heat (350F/175C). Saut the minced garlic (bawang) until golden, then add sliced onions (sibuyas) and cook until translucent. Add the native chicken pieces (native na manok) and season with crushed black pepper (durog na paminta). Add the bruised lemongrass (tanglad) and pour in the second coconut milk extract. Season with salt (asin) to taste.

Add the julienned green papaya and let it simmer until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Pour in the reserved first coconut milk extract and add the bird's eye chilies (siling labuyo) and long green chili (siling haba). Reduce heat to 300F/150C and continue to simmer until oil surfaces on top, approximately 20-30 minutes. Stir occasionally but gently to prevent the coconut milk from curdling.

For the optional traditional Bicolano niligo preparation, reserve some sauce in the pan and add day-old rice (bahaw), mixing until the rice absorbs all the flavors. Serve the Tinutungang Manok hot with steamed white rice (kanin). The dish can be stored in the refrigerator for 3-4 days in an airtight container. When reheating, use gentle heat and stir occasionally, adding extra coconut milk if needed to maintain the creamy consistency.

provided_ingredient_names: crushed black pepper durog na paminta

ingredient_line: 1 kilo pork ((use pork belly or pork loin), cut into cubes)

recipes.name: Pork Dinuguan (Pork Blood Stew) Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 kilo pork ((use pork belly or pork loin), cut into cubes)
instructions: Saute the garlic and onion in pre-heated oil until translucent.
Add the pork and cook until some of the fat from the pork has rendered.
Add water, vinegar and the pork blood. Simmer until thick or for 30 minutes.
Season the pork dinuguan with salt and pepper then add some sugar and the long green peppers. Let it simmer over low flame for 15 minutes. Serve warm.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo pork ((use pork spare rib (rib tips)), cut)

recipes.name: Taosi Spareribs Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 kilo pork ((use pork spare rib (rib tips)), cut)
instructions: Mix all the ingredients together in a bowl. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.

Steam spareribs for 50 to 60 minutes or until tender. Transfer to a serving plate and garnish with sliced leeks. Tip: You can find dried taosi black beans in Chinese delis like The Little Store, Wei Wang, and the Aranque market, and supermarkets like Unimart.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo pork (chopped to serving pieces)

recipes.name: Sinigang na Baboy sa Bayabas Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 bunch kangkong (water spinach) leaves (leaves removed from stems)
instructions: In a medium-sized stainless steel pot, boil 2 to 3 cups water. Water should slightly more than enough to cover the meat.
While the water is boiling, put the pork ribs one by one until every piece of meat is in the pot. Add the tomatoes and guava and cook for about 30 to 40 minutes or until the meat is tender.
Add the onions, gabi, labanos, salt and pepper then cook for another 8 minutes.
Then add the sitaw, okra and eggplants and simmer for another 6 minutes. Add in the kangkong and fish sauce, then let simmer for 5 minutes more. Serve hot. [ArticleReco:{"articles":["14904"]}]

ingredient_line: 1 kilo pork (gumamit ng pork belly or pork loin, hiwain)

recipes.name: Pork Dinuguan Recipe - Paano Lutuin at mga Sangkap
full_ingredients: 1 kilo pork (gumamit ng pork belly or pork loin, hiwain)
instructions: Gisahin and bawang at sibuyas sa pina-init na mantika.
Idagdag ang liempo hanggang matusta at lumabas ang sarili nitong mantika.
Ibuhos ang tubig, dugo ng baboy at suka. Tuluy-tuloy na ihalo ng 30 minuto hangga't lumapot.
Timplahan ng asin, paminta at asukal ayon sa iyong panlasa.
Ilagay ang siling pansigang at hayaang kumulo ng 15 minuto. Ihain habang mainit.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo pork (use pork picnic (kasim))

recipes.name: Asadong Matua (Old-Fashioned Pork Asado) Recipe
instructions: In a pan, sear pork kasim. If using a small pan, you can slice the meat into smaller pieces.
Remove seared meat, discard excess oil. Set aside.
In the same pan, saute onion, garlic, and tomato in medium heat. Cook tomatoes well.
Add the soy sauce and tomato sauce.
Put the meat back into the pan. Let it cook for a while with the sauce.
Add water and bring to a boil. Bring the heat down to medium and add the calamansi juice. Cover and cook until all the liquid has evaporated and the meat is tender. Season with salt and pepper.

Serve with boiled potatoes on the side. TIPS: When cooking, make sure to check on the dish once in a while you might need to add more water to make the meat tender. Also, make sure that the sauce is not gravy-like it should be a little dry.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo pork belly, slice in 1-inch cuts

recipes.name: Filipino Pork Barbecue Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 Kilo Pork Belly, slice in 1-inch cuts
1 Can lemon soda or ginger ale
Bamboo skewers pre-soak for 20 minutes before placing skewered meat
instructions: In a bowl, mixed together minced garlic, soy sauce, calamansi juice, catsup, half of the ginger ale or lemon soda, salt, black pepper.
Leave 1/2 cup of the marinade and sugar aside.
Put pork in a bowl and pour the rest of marinade.
Cover with plastic wrap, leave it for 2 hours or refrigerate overnight.
Pre-soak the bamboo skewers in hot water for 15 minutes.
Skewer the pork on a bamboo stick with up to 6 pieces per stick.
Prepare the grill and pre-heat.
Mix together 1/2 cup marinade, sugar, and remaining ginger ale or lemon soda.
Grill the pork, about 10 minutes on each side. Check constantly to avoid burning.
Total grilling time should take about 20 minutes.
Brush the pork barbecue with the marinade every few minutes to preserve the taste.
When cooked, serve hot with Atsara or Hot Rice.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo pork leg (pata)

recipes.name: Boneless Crispy Pata Recipe
instructions: Debone the pork leg then boil in water with peppercorns, salt, and bay leaves until tender, about 11/2 hours. Remove from the cooking liquid and cool.
Place pork in a deep pan filled with oil. Simmer for 20 minutes over very low heat. Set aside to cool.
Put the pork back in the oil and simmer for another 10 minutes over very low heat. Deep-fry over high heat for 5 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp.
Combine the ingredients for the soy vinaigrette: garlic, onions, soy sauce, vinegar, and bird s eye chili. Season with some salt.
Slice thinly and serve with dipping sauce and atsara.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo pork pata (sliced into serving pieces)

recipes.name: Paksiw na Pata Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 kilo pork pata (sliced into serving pieces)
instructions: Boil 5 cups of water in a large pot over medium heat. Add the pork pata and boil the pork for 10 to 15 minutes. Discard the water and clean the pork. Remove any hairs. Set aside.
Boil another 5 cups of water in the same pot. Add garlic, soy sauce, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Return the pork to the pot and simmer for 60 minutes or until the pata is tender.
Add the vinegar and simmer for 10 minutes. Add the banana blossoms. Simmer for 5 more minutes.
Add the brown sugar, and salt and pepper to taste. Simmer for 5 minutes. Serve while hot.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo pork tenderloin or butt (pigue) (sliced into large, thin slices (tapa))

recipes.name: Pork Hamonado Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 kilo pork tenderloin or butt (pigue) (sliced into large, thin slices (tapa))
1 large can pineapple (sliced and drained (around 20 ounces))
instructions: Make the marinade: combine pineapple juice, sugar, and soy sauce in a large bowl.
Marinate pork with the pineapple-soy sauce mixture for 1-3 hours.
Remove the pork from the marinade and set the remaining marinade mixture aside.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the marinated pork until the meat turns light brown (approximately 3 to 5 minutes).
Pour in the remaining marinade mixture together with the pineapple slices, water, and liquid pork seasoning and simmer for 45 to 60 minutes.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Slice the pork loin before serving and serve with pineapple slices and sauce.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo sarangani bay boneless milkfish belly

recipes.name: Bangus Belly Bistek
full_ingredients: 1 kilo SARANGANI BAY Boneless Milkfish Belly
instructions: Heat oil and saute garlic until golden brown. Add onion and cook until translucent. Add tomatoes and cook until mushy. Add soy-calamansi mixture. Add milkfish bellies, one at a time. Add water. Boil and cover for 2 minutes. Add pepper. Reduce and simmer until bellies are cooked firm.
Top with onion rings. Serve with steaming rice.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo squid (pusit) (naka-slice at nakahiwalay ang squid ink)

recipes.name: Adobong Pusit Recipe (Tagalog Version)
full_ingredients: 1 kilo Squid (Pusit) (naka-slice at nakahiwalay ang squid ink)
instructions: Igisa ang bawang at sibuyas sa kawaling may mantika.
Idagdag ang mga nahiwang pusit kasama ng tinta ng pusit at tubig. Pakuluin ito nang 2 minuto hanggang malutong mabuti ang pusit.
Idagdag ang toyo at suka. Timplahan ng asin at paminta.
Hayaang kumulo nang 2-3 minuto o hanggang sa maging malapot ang sarsa.

ingredient_line: 1 kilo tilapia (use fillet)

recipes.name: Crispy Tilapia Sticks Recipe
instructions: Make the coating: Mix the flour, cornstarch, salt and pepper. Set aside.
Dredge the tilapia fillet in the flour mixture.
Fry the fillets one by one in oil until golden brown. Remove from the pan and drain the excess oil using paper towels.
Serve with sweet chili or spicy chili sauce.

ingredient_line: 1 kilogram beef (cubed large)

recipes.name: Cheesy Kaldereta Recipe
full_ingredients: 4 pieces green and red bell peppers (seeded, cut into strips)
2 medium carrots (peeled, cut into large chunks)
1/2 185-gram block quickmelt cheese (grated, more to serve)
instructions: Mag-init ng mantika sa pressure cooker. Ilagay ang sibuyas at lutuin hangga t lumambot. Ilagay ang baka, ang mga bell peppers, at ang sabaw galing baka. Magdagdag ng sabaw kung kulang ito. Pakuluin ang sabaw bago takpan at isara ang pressure cooker. Hayaan kumulo ang baka hanggang maging malambot ang mga ito (mga isa t hanggang dalawang oras kumukulo).

Pag malambot na ang baka, ihalo ang tomato sauce at toyo at ilagay din ang patatas, carrot, at siling pangsigang bago pakuluin muli ang sabaw. Hayaan matuyo ang sabaw hanggang maging malapot ng kaunti ang sabaw at maging malambot ang mga patatas at carrot.

Idagdag sa kaldero ang dinurog na keso at hayaan matunaw sa sarsa. Pakuluin ang sarsa ulit hanggang magiging malapot ang sarsa. Pasarapin gamit ang asin at pamintang durong. Ihanda ang kalderetang baka kasama ang sinaing na kanin.

ingredient_line: 1 kilogram chicken pieces (thighs and wings or adodo cut)

recipes.name: Chicken Bistek Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 kilogram chicken pieces (thighs and wings or adodo cut)
instructions: In a large bowl combine soy sauce, calamansi juice, garlic, salt, and pepper then add the chicken pieces. Set aside to let marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat, pour in oil and fry onion slices. Set aside. Lower heat to medium-low heat.
In the same pan, add chicken pieces then pour in the marinade. Add water and simmer for 20 minutes or until chicken is cooked through. Remove from heat. Add onions before serving.

ingredient_line: 1 kilogram pork kasim (hiniwa sa 1-pulgadang kuwadrado)

recipes.name: Pinoy-Style Pork Barbecue Recipe - Paano Lutuin At Mga Sangkap
instructions: Gawin ang panimpla: Sa isang malaking mangkok, paghaluin ang banana ketchup, soysauce, liquid seasoning, bawang, katas ng kalamansi, pamintang durog, asukal na pula, lime-flavored softdrinks, at hot sauce.
Itusok na mabuti ang karne sa barbecue stick. Maaring lagyan ng isang pirasong taba ng baboy sa dulo ng bawat barbecue, kung nais.

Sa isang lalagyan, ayusin ang mga naituhog na karne sa dalawang hilera. Magtabi ng isang tasa ng ginawang panimpla para sa pampahid sa pag-ihaw. Ilagay ang natitirang panimpla sa mga naituhog na karne at ibabad magdamag habang nasa loob ng refrigerator.
Gawin ang sarsang pamahid: Sa isang mangkok, ilagay ang itinabing panimpla at haluan ng mantika.
Ilagay ang naituhog na barbecue sa ihawan para ihawin. Pahiran ng sarsa ang karne paminsan minsan upang hindi matuyo habang niluluto. Ihawin hanggang sa maluto ang loob ng karne. Ihain habang mainit.

ingredient_line: 1 kilogram pork tenderloin ((gumamit ng parteng lomo o pige), hiwain ng malapad at manipis (tapa))

recipes.name: Pork Hamonado Recipe - Paano Lutuin At Mga Sangkap
full_ingredients: 1 kilogram pork tenderloin ((gumamit ng parteng lomo o pige), hiwain ng malapad at manipis (tapa))
1 large can canned pineapples (sinala, humigit kumulang 20 onsa)
instructions: Gawin ang pangtimpla: paghaluin ang katas ng pinya, asukal na pula at soy sauce sa isang malaking mangkok.
Ibabad ang baboy sa halong katas ng pinya sa loob ng 1-3 oras.
Alisin ang karne mula sa pinagbabaran at itabi ang natitirang pangtimpla.
Painitan ang mantika sa kawali at iprito ang tinimplahang karne hanggang sa maging light brown ang kulay (humigit-kumulang 3-5 minuto).
Ibuhos ang natitirang pangtimpla kasama ang hiwang pinya, tubig at liquid seasoning at pakuluan sa loob ng 45-60 minuto.
Lagyan ng asin at paminta ayon sa panlasa.
Hiwain ang karne bago ihain. Lagyan ng mga hiwang pinya at sarsa.

ingredient_line: 1 kilogram squid (cleaned and ink removed)

recipes.name: Adobong Pusit Without Ink Recipe
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat, and saute the onions, garlic, and tomato until fragrant.
Add in the squid then pour the vinegar and let simmer for 2 minutes. Do not stir.
Lower the heat and add in the soy sauce, green chili, and water. Cook for another 10 to 15 minutes. Serve while hot.

ingredient_line: 1 kilogram` chicken (cut into pieces)

recipes.name: Chop Suey with Chicken Recipe
instructions: Marinate chicken in soy sauce for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Saute onion and garlic until fragrant. Add longganisang Macau and saute for 1 minute. Add chicken and marinade. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add fish sauce and water. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add carrots, cauliflower, celery, green beans, snow peas, and young corn. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Add pechay Baguio. Simmer for 1 minute.
Add dissolved cornstarch and simmer until sauce is thick. Serve hot.

ingredient_line: 1 large boneless bangus milkfish; scales removed, cleaned and butterflied

recipes.name: Fried Bangus Recipe (Fried Milkfish)
full_ingredients: 1 large boneless bangus milkfish; scales removed, cleaned and butterflied
instructions: Combine vinegar, garlic, whole peppercorn, and salt in a bowl. Stir.
In a deep wide plate, pour-in the mixture and then lay down the fish in a manner that the sliced part is facing down (skin should face up). Cover and place in the fridge. Marinate for 8 to 12 hours.

Heat the cooking oil in a pan. Fry both sides of the bangus in medium heat until the color turns medium brown (note: it should take around 5 minutes per side). Note: the oil has a tendency to splatter because of the liquid from the marinade. Make sure to cover the pan while leaving open a small space for the steam to escape.
Serve with spiced vinegar (sinamak).
Share and enjoy!

ingredient_line: 1 large bundle chinese cabbage/pechay pechay baguio

recipes.name: Filipino Bulalo (Bone Marrow Soup)
full_ingredients: 3 lbs beef shanks with bone marrow buto-buto
1 large bundle Chinese cabbage/pechay pechay Baguio
2 green onions cut into 2-inch lengths (sibuyas dahon)
instructions: Thoroughly clean the beef shanks under running water (Hugasan mabuti ang buto-buto). Fill a large pot with cold water and add the cleaned beef shanks. Bring the water to a full boil (Pakuluan hanggang kumulo) - this will take about 10 minutes.
Once boiling, drain the water and rinse both the pot and the meat to remove impurities (Hugasan ang kaldero at karne). This first boiling helps achieve a clear broth later.

Return the cleaned meat to the pot and add fresh cold water until the meat is completely covered (Lagyan ng sapat na tubig). Add the quartered onions, whole peppercorns, and fish sauce (Idagdag ang sibuyas, paminta, at patis). Bring to a boil again, then immediately reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer at 85-90C/185-195F (Ibaba ang apoy at pakuluan ng banayad).

Let the broth simmer gently for 2 to 2.5 hours (Pakuluan ng dahan-dahan ng dalawang oras), occasionally skimming any foam or impurities that rise to the surface (Alisin ang bumubula sa ibabaw). The meat should be tender but still holding its shape when pierced with a fork (Kapag malambot na ang karne pero hindi pa nagkakadurug-durog).

After the meat is tender, add the quartered potatoes and corn (Idagdag ang patatas at mais). Continue simmering for 10-15 minutes until the potatoes are almost cooked through (Pakuluan hanggang malambot ang patatas).
Add the celery pieces (Idagdag ang kintsay) and cook for another 3-5 minutes. The celery should retain some crunch (May crunch pa dapat ang kintsay).

Finally, add the pechay and green onions (Idagdag ang pechay at dahon ng sibuyas). Cook for just 2-3 minutes until the vegetables are bright green and crisp-tender (Hanggang lumambot ng kaunti ang gulay).
Taste the broth and adjust seasoning with salt as needed (Timplahan ng asin kung kinakailangan). The soup should be savory but not too salty, as diners can add more fish sauce to taste.

Serve hot in large, deep bowls (Ihain ng mainit sa malalaking mangkok). Place small dishes of fish sauce, calamansi, and chopped Thai chilies on the table so each person can season their portion to taste (Lagyan ng sawsawan: patis, kalamansi, at siling labuyo). Always serve with hot steamed rice (Ihain kasama ang mainit na kanin).

For the traditional way of eating bulalo, encourage diners to scoop out the bone marrow and add it to their rice or soup. The marrow can be seasoned with a little patis and calamansi for extra flavor (Masarap timplahan ng patis at kalamansi).

ingredient_line: 1 large carrot (hiniwa ng 1/2 pulgada pabilog)

recipes.name: Pork Belly with Crackling Skin Recipe - Paano Lutuin At Mga Sangkap
full_ingredients: 2 kilograms pork (gumamit ng parte ng tiyan ng baboy na may kasamang buto)
3 stalks celery (hiniwa sa 2 pulgada na haba)
instructions: Timplahan ang pork belly ng asin at paminta. Takpan ng aluminium foil at ilagay sa refrigerator magdamag.
Painitin ang oven sa 350 degrees F.
Ilagay ang karot, celery at tanglad sa isang roasting pan na kakasya ang pork belly. Ilagay ang karne na nakaibabaw ang balat sa ibabaw ng mga gulay.

Ilagay ang pan sa gitna ng oven at i-roast sa loob ng 2 1/2 - 3 oras o hanggang sa ang init kapag nilagyan ng meat thermometer ang karne ay umabot sa 135-140 degrees F. Itaas ang temperature sa 420 degrees at ipagpatuloy ang pagluluto habang paminsan paminsang pinapahiran ng tumulong mantika sa loob ng 10-12 minuto o hanggang sa maging brown ang balat.
Tanggalin ang pan sa oven at hayaan ang karne sa loob ng 15 minuto. Buhusan ng kumukulong mantika ang balat para mag-sizzle.
Hayaan muna sa loob ng 10 minuto bago hiwain. Ihain kasama ang applesauce pangsawsawan.

ingredient_line: 1 large carrot carrot, finely shredded

recipes.name: Rellenong Manok (Filipino Stuffed Chicken)
full_ingredients: 1 whole chicken 4-5 lbs - Use air-chilled for better texture
1/2 cup calamansi juice or lemon juice
instructions: Begin by deboning the chicken at room temperature (25C). Place chicken breast-side down and carefully separate meat from bones while keeping skin intact (Ilagay ang manok nang pataob at maingat na ihiwalay ang laman sa buto habang iniingatan ang balat). Reserve carcass for stock.

Mix marinade of calamansi juice, soy sauce, and pepper. Marinate chicken in refrigerator (4C) for 1 hour (Ihalo ang katas ng kalamansi, toyo, at paminta. Ibabad ang manok ng isang oras sa refrigerator).

While chicken marinates, prepare the stuffing (Ihanda ang palaman): Combine ground pork, drained crushed pineapple, grated onion, shredded carrot, breadcrumbs, cheese, raisins, banana ketchup, beaten eggs, salt, and pepper. Mix thoroughly but gently. Keep mixture cold, below 4C (Paghaluin nang maingat ang lahat ng sangkap at panatilihing malamig).

Pat marinated chicken dry. Stuff with half the meat mixture, place hard-boiled eggs in center, then add remaining stuffing (Punasan ang manok at ilagay ang kalahating bahagi ng palaman, ilagay ang matigas na itlog sa gitna, at idagdag ang natitirang palaman). Sew openings closed and tie legs together.
Preheat oven to 190C (375F). Brush chicken with mayonnaise (Pahiran ng mayonnaise ang manok). Place in roasting pan and cook for 1.5 hours (Ilagay sa roasting pan at lutuin ng 1.5 oras).

In the final 20 minutes, baste with melted butter (Sa huling 20 minuto, pahiran ng tunaw na mantikilya). Check internal temperature reaches 74C (165F) for food safety (Siguraduhing umabot sa 74C ang init sa loob).
Let rest for 15 minutes before slicing (Palamigin ng 15 minuto bago hiwahin). When reheating, ensure temperature reaches 74C (165F) throughout.

recipes.name: Chicken Afritada Recipe
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a pan.
Saute potatoes, carrots and bell pepper and set aside
Using the same pan, saute garlic and onion
Add the Chicken
Simmer for 10-15 minutes or until tender. (requires occasional stirring).

Bring to a boil.

Adjust according to taste

ingredient_line: 1 large fish 1 to 2 lbs, cleaned and salted

recipes.name: Fish Escabeche Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 large fish 1 to 2 lbs, cleaned and salted
1 medium red bell pepper sliced into strips
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a frying pan then fry both sides of the fish until a bit crispy. Set aside.
Heat a clean pan and pour-in the vinegar. Let boil.

Put-in the onion and red bell pepper. Stir and cook until the vegetables are tender.

ingredient_line: 1 large onion chopped (isang malaking sibuyas, hiniwa)

recipes.name: Adobong Manok sa Patis (Filipino Chicken Adobo with Fish Sauce)
full_ingredients: 1 whole chicken 3-4 pounds, cut into serving pieces (1 buong manok)
1 whole head garlic minced (isang buong buo ng bawang, dinurog)
1 large onion chopped (isang malaking sibuyas, hiniwa)
1/2 teaspoon whole black peppercorns crushed (pamintang buo, dinurog)
instructions: Begin by heating your pot over medium heat and adding oil. Once hot, toss in your chopped onions and minced garlic. Cook them until the onions turn clear and soft - this takes about 3-4 minutes.
Now add your chicken pieces to the pot. Let them cook and brown on each side for about 5-7 minutes, turning them occasionally. You want them to get a nice light golden color.
Pour in the fish sauce and let it bubble for 2 minutes, occasionally moving the chicken around to coat it well. This step is important as it helps reduce the strong fish sauce smell.
Add the vinegar and - this is important - don't stir it! Let it boil without touching it for 3-5 minutes. This prevents the vinegar from becoming bitter.

Pour in the water, add your bay leaves and crushed peppercorns. Turn the heat to low, cover the pot, and let everything simmer gently for 20-25 minutes. You'll know it's ready when the chicken is tender enough to easily cut with a fork.

Give it a taste and add a little salt if needed. Let it rest for 5-10 minutes before serving - this helps all the flavors come together beautifully. Your adobo should have a perfect balance of sour and savory flavors, making it ideal for spooning over a plate of hot rice.
Remember: the sauce will continue to develop flavor as it sits, so it's even better the next day!

ingredient_line: 1 large orange sweet potatoes (kamote) ((kamoteng kahel), peeled, cut into sticks)

recipes.name: Lumpiang Gulay Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 large orange sweet potatoes (kamote) ((kamoteng kahel), peeled, cut into sticks)
1 large sweet potatoes (kamote) (peeled, cut into sticks)
1 bunch green beans or Baguio beans (sliced diagonally)
instructions: Initin ang mantika sa isang malaking kawali. Ilagay at gisahin ang tokwa hanggang maluto ito y maluto. Itabi ang lutong tokwa.

Ilagay ang hiwang kamoteng kahel at lutuin din ito hanggang lumambot. Ilagay ang lutong kamote sa lalagyan kasama ang tokwa. Lutuin din ang kamoteng puti sa mainit na mantika. Isama sa lutong kamoteng kahel at tokwa. Itabi ang mga ito.
Bawasan ang mantika hanggang ang natirang mantika sa kawali ay kasya sa paggisa. Ilagay at gisahin ang sibuyas. Isunod ang bawang at gisahin rin ito hanggang ito y maging malambot.
Idagdag sa kawali ang sitaw at repolyo. Gisahin nang mabuti hanggang ito y malanta sa init ng kawali. Ibalik ang mga lutong tokwa at kamote sa kawali at haluin nang mabuti.
Timplahan ang ginisang gulay gamit ang patis at durog na paminta, ayon sa iyong panlasa. Haluin ulit ang mga gulay. Patayin ang kalan at palamigin ang nalutong gulay.

Maglagay ng isang lumpia wrapper sa sangkalan. Maglagay ng isa hanggang tatlong kutsarang gulay sa lumpia wrapper. Pahiran ng itlog ang dulo ng lumpia wrapper. Irolyo ang ang lumpia wrapper na may gulay sa loob. Pahiran muli ng itlog kung kailangan para maisara nang mahigpit ang lumpia. Itabi ang gawang lumpia at ulitin ang prosesong ito sa pagbalot sa natitirang gulay at lumpia wrapper.

Pag handa nang iluto ang mga lumpia, initin muli ang mantika sa isang kawali na pang prito. Maglagay ng hanggang limang lumpia sa mainit na mantika at lutuin ang mga ito hanggang maging malutong ang wrapper at uminit muli ang gulay sa loob na lumpia. Itabi sa isang patuluan o rack para hindi lumambot o maging mamantika ang mga lutong lumpia. Lutuin ang mga natitirang lumpia.
Gawin ang sawsawan: Haluin nang mabuti sa isang lalagyan ang toyo, suka, bawang, at asukal. Ihain ang lumpia kasama ang ginawang sawsawan.

ingredient_line: 1 large pizza dough

recipes.name: Sisig Pizza
full_ingredients: 1 medium yellow onion sliced crosswise into rings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400.
Meanwhile, place the pizza though in a flat surface. Pour the Alfredo sauce over the pizza though and spread it all throughout equally.
Arrange the sisig over the Alfredo sauce. This is best done using your hands (it will be better if you wear plastic gloves during the process).
Arrange the onion and sliced finger chili on top. Sprinkle chili flakes all over the pizza.
Put the pizza in the oven. Bake for 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven. Slice.
Serve. Share and enjoy!

ingredient_line: 1 large pompano pampano, cleaned, gutted, and scored

recipes.name: Pinangat na Isda (Filipino Sour Fish Stew)
full_ingredients: 1 large pompano Pampano, cleaned, gutted, and scored
Choice of souring agent: 4 tablespoons tamarind powder Sampalok, 8 pieces bilimbi (Kamias) or 1/2 cup calamansi or lemon juice
3 stalks spring onions Dahon ng Sibuyas, chopped
instructions: Start by thoroughly cleaning the pompano fish. Score the skin on both sides with diagonal cuts. Season the fish generously with salt and ground black pepper, making sure to season the inside cavity too.

Heat enough oil in a wok for shallow frying over medium-high heat. Once hot, carefully place the fish and fry until golden brown and crispy on both sides, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove the fish and set aside.

Pour out most of the oil, leaving about 3 tablespoons in the wok. Add minced garlic, sliced shallots, and minced ginger. Saut over medium heat until fragrant and shallots are softened, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they start to soften, about 4 minutes. If using bilimbi (kamias), add them now and gently mash with your spoon as they cook.

Pour in 11/2 cups of water and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, cover the wok, and let it simmer for 3 minutes. If you're using bilimbi, give it an extra 3 minutes of simmering to extract more sourness.
Place the fried fish back into the wok. If you're using tamarind powder or calamansi juice instead of bilimbi, add it now. Let everything simmer on low heat for 5 minutes.
Carefully flip the fish over and continue simmering for 2 more minutes. Taste the broth if it's too sour, add a little water. Season with fish sauce and more black pepper if needed.
Add the chopped spring onions and simmer for a final 2 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it rest for 2-3 minutes before serving.
Serve hot with steamed rice. Place extra fish sauce, chopped chilies, and calamansi on the side so everyone can adjust the flavors to their taste.

Note: You can control the sourness by adjusting the amount of souring agent (bilimbi, tamarind powder, or calamansi) to your preference. The broth should be more concentrated and less soupy than sinigang.

ingredient_line: 1 large red apple (peeled, cut into medium cubes (the spongy, not crunchy type))

recipes.name: Mechado ala Alejandrino
full_ingredients: 1/4 kilo pork fat (cut into large cubes)
1 kilo cow cheeks (cut in desired serving sizes)
1 large red apple (peeled, cut into medium cubes (the spongy, not crunchy type))
1 medium red bell pepper (cut into large cubes)
instructions: Sweat onion, garlic, and tomatoes in olive oil. Add bay leaves, peppercorns, salt, and sugar, and cook until onion and tomatoes are quite mushy.
Saute and render the pork fat. Increase fire a bit and add cow cheeks. Allow cow cheeks to cook for about 5 minutes until it turns a darker shade. Add enough stock to cover.
When meat is halfway cooked, add the apple cubes.
Simmer until beef is tender and sauce is thick.
Add bell peppers and olives, and simmer for another 5 minutes.

ingredient_line: 1 large talong eggplant/solanum melongena, cut into 1-inch wedges

recipes.name: Paksiw na Bangus (Filipino Milkfish in Vinegar Stew)
full_ingredients: 1 large bangus milkfish/Chanos chanos, about 1 kg
1 large talong eggplant/Solanum melongena, cut into 1-inch wedges
4 butil ng bawang garlic cloves, crushed
instructions: First, start by cleaning the bangus. Remove the innards and gently wash the fish, keeping the scales on if you prefer. Cut the fish crosswise into 2-inch thick slices.
Crush 4 cloves of garlic and slice one thumb-sized piece of ginger into strips. Cut one large eggplant into 1-inch thick wedges. Slice one onion thinly.
Take your cooking pot or kawali and layer the sliced onions, crushed garlic, and ginger strips at the bottom.
Place the bangus pieces on top of these aromatics. Try not to stack or overlap the fish pieces. Arrange the eggplant wedges and finger chilies around the fish.
Pour 1/2 cup vinegar and 1 cup water over everything. Add 11/2 teaspoons salt and 1 teaspoon whole peppercorns. Do not stir.
Turn the heat to high and let it come to a boil. Once boiling, lower the heat and cover the pot. Let it simmer gently for 15 minutes. Remember not to stir, as this will break the fish.
After 15 minutes, check if the fish is cooked through. The flesh should be opaque and flaky.
Here's the special step that makes this recipe perfect: drizzle 1 teaspoon of cooking oil over the top. Instead of stirring, gently shake the pot to spread the oil.
Let everything simmer for 2-3 more minutes, then turn off the heat. Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve hot with rice and fish sauce on the side. This dish tastes even better the next day, after the flavors have had time to develop.

recipes.name: Sinuglaw

2 cups cucumber seeded and thinly sliced
1 1/4 cup vinegar cane, white, or coconut vinegar
4 to 6 pieces Thai or Birds eye chili chopped
instructions: Place the tuna meat in a bowl then pour-in 1/2 cup of vinegar. Soak for 8 minutes.

recipes.name: Spicy Camaron Rebosado (Deep Fried Beer Battered Shrimp)
full_ingredients: 1 lb. medium or large shrimp deveined and shell removed
instructions: Heat oil in a pot.
Beat the egg in a bowl.
Add ground black pepper, garlic powder, salt, and cayenne pepper.
Pour the beer. Whisk until the ingredients are well blended.
Add half of the flour. Continue to whisk until the texture becomes smooth. Add the remaining flour and whisk some more.
Put the baking powder in the bowl. Stir until well blended.

Dip the shrimp in the batter. Gently drop on the pot with oil and then deep fry for 2 minutes. Roll the shrimp over and continue to deep fry for 1 minute. Remove the fried beer battered shrimp and place in a plate topped with a paper towel. Perform this step until all the shrimp are cooked.
Transfer to a serving plate. Serve with ponzu or sweet and sour sauce.
Share and enjoy!

2 bunches bok choy lower end cut
Salt and ground black pepper to taste

Saut garlic onion, and tomato
Once the onion becomes tender, add the Chinese sausage and pork belly. Continue to cook until the pork belly browns (around 3 minutes).
Pour the tomato sauce and water. Let boil.
Add the pork (or beef cubes). Stir. Cover the pot and set the heat to low. Boil for 50 minutes.

Combine AP flour and cornstarch. Mix well and then set aside.
Put the shrimp in the same bowl. Marinade for at least 30 minutes.

ingredient_line: 1 liter cola (left out until flat)

recipes.name: Davao Humba Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 to 2 bunches Taiwan pechay (steamed or blanched)
1/3 Cup Vinegar ((use sukang pinakurat), to serve)
instructions: Toast cinnamon and star anise in a dry pan over low heat until fragrant. Set aside.
Using a mortar and pestle, pound garlic, peppercorns, cilantro root, and cilantro leaves and stems together until paste-like in consistency.
Heat a heavy-bottomed pot or casserole over medium-high heat. Add 4 cups water, cola, oyster sauce, garlic mixture, cinnamon, and star anise. Bring to a boil.
Add pork. Season with salt. Lower heat and simmer until pork is tender, about 21/2 to 3 hours. (The meat will become juicy and sticky.) Add more water, if necessary.
Transfer pork to a serving plate. Serve with pechay, eggs, and pinakurat for dipping.

ingredient_line: 1 long cinnamon stick

recipes.name: Lamb Curry
instructions: Melt butter in a medium saucepot. Add cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and star anise. Fry over low heat until fragrant. Add shallots and saute until transparent. Add garlic and ginger and saute until fragrant.

Mix Kurma curry powder with a little water to make a paste. Add curry paste to the pan and saute for a few seconds. Add lamb cubes and cook meat for 5 minutes until browned. Add chicken stock and coconut milk and mix well; simmer until meat becomes tender, about 25 minutes. Add potatoes and continue to simmer until potatoes are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add yogurt and mix well. Add mint or cilantro and season to taste with salt. Simmer for another 5 minutes. Serve with basmati rice, if desired.

ingredient_line: 1 medim bittermelon (sliced)

recipes.name: Grilled Pinakbet Recipe

1 bunch winged beans (sigarilyas) (sliced into bite-sized pieces)

Make the bagoong-yogurt dressing: mix bottled bagoong, calamansi juice, green finger chili, olive oil, and yogurt in a bowl.
Place shrimps, vegetables, and katuray on a platter. Drizzle with desired dressing or serve dressings on the side.

ingredient_line: 1 medium bangus (butterflied, deboned, scales removed)

recipes.name: Inihaw Na Bangus Recipe
full_ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper (or to taste)
instructions: Mix patis, calamansi juice, onion, tomatoes, and ginger, and set aside. Season the milkfish with salt and pepper. Rub salt on all sides of the fish.
On a flat surface, lay the foil or banana leaves and place the fish on top of the fool or banana leaves skin side down. Top the fish with the onion and tomato mixture.
Add salted eggs and kesong puti on top of the onion and tomato mixture. Wrap the fish in foil or banana leaves. Make sure that the fish is covered with foil or banana leaves.

Prepare the grill by heating the charcoal. Cook the fish over High Heat for 15 minutes on each side. If a grill is not available, cook the fish in a dry wok over medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes on each side. Garnish the fish with wansoy before serving.

ingredient_line: 1 medium bunch baguio pechay (chopped)

recipes.name: Hinalang Recipe
full_ingredients: 1 kilo Beef ((use shanks), sliced into 2-inch pieces)
instructions: Heat oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or casserole over medium heat. Saute onions, garlic, ginger, red pepper, and green onions until lightly browned and fragrant. Season with salt and pepper.

Add chilies and stir. Add beef in one layer. Add 8 cups water and season with salt. Lower heat and simmer until beef is tender, about 2 to 3 hours. Add more water, if necessary. Remove impurities that rise to the surface. Add pechay and cook for 2 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

ingredient_line: 1 medium cucumber (tinanggal ang buto, hiniwa pahaba)

recipes.name: California Maki Recipe - Paano Lutuin At Mga Sangkap
full_ingredients: 2 cups Japanese rice (bigas na maliliit ang butil)
1 medium Cucumber (tinanggal ang buto, hiniwa pahaba)
instructions: Paghaluin ang suka, asukal at asin.
Kapag luto na ang kanin, ilagay ito sa isang maliit na mangkok.

Ibuhos ang tinimplang suka sa kanin at haluin gamit ang isang kahoy na sandok. Habang hinahalo ay importanteng paypayan ang kanin upang lumamig. Ito ang makakapagpakintab sa kanin at maiiwasang ang pagiging malabsak. Takpan ng mamasa-masang tela at itabi.

Ihanda ang roll: Ilapat ang sushi mat sa lamesa. Hatiin ang nori at ilagay sa ibabang bahagi ng sushi mat. Bahagyang basain ang inyong kamay at kumuha ng kaunting kanin. Ikalat ang kanin sa nori. Budburan ng masago at ikalat ng pantay sa kanin. Baligtarin ang nagawang kanin na may budbod ng masago.
Habang nakaharap pababa ang kanin at masago, ilatag ang manga, kani at pipino sa ibaba ng nori.

Para mai-rolyo, ilagay ang hinlalaki sa ilalim ng bamboo mat at gamitin ito para maiangat ang mat at kanin sa ibabaw ng palaman, habang ginagamit ang ibang daliri para hawakan ito. Gamitin ang sushi mat para mairolyo hanggang sa dulo ng nori.
Diinan ang sushi mat para humigpit ang rolyo. Dahan-dahan itong tanggalin sa sushi mat. Gumamit ng matalas na kutsilyo upang hiwain ang sushi roll.

ingredient_line: 1 medium kalabasa squash/pumpkin, cut into 2-inch chunks

recipes.name: Authentic Pinakbet Tagalog (Filipino Vegetable Stew)
full_ingredients: 500 g pork belly liempo, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 medium kalabasa squash/pumpkin, cut into 2-inch chunks
1 bundle sitaw yard-long beans, cut into 3-inch lengths
1 medium ampalaya bitter gourd, seeded and sliced
instructions: Heat your kawali or large pot over medium heat (180C/350F). Pour mantika (cooking oil) and wait until it becomes hot but not smoking. Igisa ang bawang (saut the minced garlic) until it turns light golden brown and releases its aroma, this should take about 30 seconds. Add the chopped sibuyas (onions) into the pan and continue cooking until they become malinaw (translucent), which takes about 2-3 minutes.

Add the cubed liempo (pork belly) to the pan and increase the heat to medium-high (190C/375F). Let the meat cook until it becomes lightly browned or kulay-kayumanggi on all sides, this will take around 5-7 minutes. Stir occasionally to ensure even cooking. Add the bagoong alamang (shrimp paste) to the pork and mix well, allowing it to cook for 2 more minutes to enhance its flavor.

Add the quartered kamatis (tomatoes) to the pan and reduce heat back to medium (180C/350F). Allow the tomatoes to soften and release their juice or magbuga ng katas, cooking them for about 3-4 minutes. Pour the tubig (water) into the pot and wait for it to reach a gentle boil. Once boiling, lower the heat (150C/300F), cover the pot, and let it simmer until the pork becomes malambot (tender), which should take approximately 15-20 minutes.

Now begins the careful process of adding your gulay (vegetables). First, add the chunks of kalabasa (squash) to the pot and let them cook for 5 minutes at medium-low heat (160C/320F). Next, add the cut sitaw (long beans) and continue cooking for 3 minutes. Add your sliced talong (eggplant) and ampalaya (bitter gourd) to the pot and cook for another 3 minutes. Finally, add the okra and let everything cook together for 2-3 more minutes.

Timplahan ng asin at paminta (season with salt and pepper) according to your taste. Haluing maingat (gently stir) all the ingredients to combine the flavors while being careful not to break the vegetables. The vegetables should be malutong-malambot (tender-crisp) when done. Your pinakbet is ready when the sauce has slightly reduced but remains sabaw (saucy), the vegetables are cooked but still hold their shape, and the pork is fork-tender.

Let the dish rest for 5 minutes before serving. This allows the flavors to settle and the sauce to thicken slightly. Serve your pinakbet hot with mainit na kanin (steaming rice). For the best experience, place a small bowl of patis (fish sauce) on the table to allow each person to adjust the saltiness to their preference.

For storing any leftovers, let the pinakbet cool completely to room temperature or malamig-lamig. Transfer to a lalagyang hindi papasukan ng hangin (airtight container) and keep in the refrigerator. When reheating, add a splash of tubig (water) and warm gently over medium heat until the dish is mainit (hot) throughout, usually taking about 5-7 minutes. Avoid overheating to prevent the vegetables from becoming too soft or malambot.
